post.title: Galaxy Sandbox: Sessions as Galaxies
post.hook: Every Claude Code session on your machine, rendered as its own spinning galaxy.
post.summary: A React and Canvas 2D galaxy simulation where thousands of stars orbit softened-gravity cores. Its default scene turns local Claude Code sessions into inspectable, promptable galaxies.
post.writeup:
## What it is
Galaxy Sandbox is an interactive particle simulation. Thousands of stars orbit galaxy cores under softened gravity. Close passes pull spiral arms into tidal tails, and slow encounters merge cores.

## Why it exists
Besides the physics scenes (Trio, Collision, Binary, Cluster, Solo), it opens on a Sessions scene. Every Claude Code session on your machine becomes a galaxy, sized by message count and colored by project. The session you launched from sits at the center in lime.

## How it works
The engine in `src/engine/sim.ts` integrates particles with semi-implicit Euler, storing them in typed arrays per galaxy. In sandbox scenes, cores attract each other and merge while conserving momentum. In the Sessions scene, cores follow prescribed golden-angle orbits, and each star feels only its own core, so dozens of galaxies stay cheap. Rendering is Canvas 2D with additive blending, and trails come from fading the previous frame. React only drives the HUD, the inspect card and the activity poller.

Session data comes from a small Vite middleware that reads `~/.claude/projects/*/`. The browser calls `GET /api/sessions` and `POST /api/prompt`, and the server does the file reads and process spawn, so no paths or credentials reach the client.

## What you can do
- Click a galaxy to see its project, title, message count, transcript size and last-active time.
- Prompt it headlessly with `claude --resume <id> -p "<prompt>"`, keeping the same transcript.
- Sessions written in the last 90 seconds get a pulsing core, a faster orbit and a green dot.
- Sessions written in the last 20 seconds are treated as live elsewhere and are not resumed.

## Open questions
The current session cannot be prompted from the UI. Prompting also depends on the `claude` CLI being logged in, or the resumed session records a 401.
